newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends mostly up on cash, spillover.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends mostly up on cash, spillover.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended mostly higher on strength in the domestic market and on spillover from other U.S. wheat markets, traders said.
"Our cash markets are firming up again, but mostly we were just following the other markets," a MGE source said.
Wheat gained early on bullish export data and extended those gains after the EU granted refunds on wheat for exports, traders said.
The EU said Thursday it granted 350,500 tonnes of free-market soft wheat at a refund of 22.35 ECUs per tonne. Traders had expected a refund of between 23 and 25 ECUs.

Wheat gained early after the USDA released its weekly export report, which was perceived as bullish for corn, beans and wheat. Wheat also gained on further short-covering tied to signs the market was oversold.
MGE spring wheat closed one cent per bushel lower to 3-3/4 cents higher, with Dec up 3-3/4 cents at $3.85-1/4.

Traders said volumes were mainly light, although locals were buying the spread. Benson-Quinn bull-spread at least 700,000 Dec/March bushels. Atwood peavey bear-spread 7700,000 March/Dec. Atwood-Peavey sold 1.2 million Dec bushels.
The Dec/March spread was said to have widened to trade at 13-1/2 cents late from 12 cents early.
MGE barley futures closed three to 12 cents per cwt higher, with Dec up 12 cents at $6.42.
